title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla defends Steelers fandom amid criticism
content:
Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla took to social media Friday to defend his Pittsburgh Steelers fandom that dates back 50 years.

After NFL owners unanimously approved the sale of the Seahawks to Vinod and Neeru Khosla on Wednesday, Vinod Khosla revealed at an introductory news conference that he has been, and still is, a fan of the Steelers since his arrival in the U.S. in 1976.

Two days later, he provided a lengthy response to a post on X from Barstool Sports criticizing his comments about rooting for Pittsburgh.

“Reporters will make every molehill into a mountain just to get column inches to write or video minutes,” Khosla said. “What’s wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited about the NFL? I still watch their games doesn’t mean I won’t unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the @Seahawks to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!! Zero questions!!!

“At the other end is a set of teams I always want to lose every advantage. But happy to have the sports writer getting more column inches and fill their pages. You are welcome. Apologies in advance for my very transparent style.”

On July 11, the Seahawks announced the Paul G. Allen estate had reached an agreement with the Khoslas to sell the franchise for an NFL-record $9.612 billion. Allen’s sister, Jody Allen, had operated the team since Paul died in 2018. The Allens were famously elusive during their tenures running the team, rarely making public comments.

Vinod was born in India and immigrated to the U.S. to continue his education, attending Carnegie Mellon in Pittsburgh. He is considered one of Silicon Valley’s most influential innovators and venture capitalists.

Neeru Khosla will be the controlling owner of the Seahawks. Their son, Neal, is also expected to have a major role.

On Wednesday, Vinod said the family is committed to keeping the Seahawks Super Bowl contenders. A day later, the franchise made its first significant move under the family’s ownership, agreeing to a contract extension with Pro Bowl defensive tackle Leonard Williams that runs through 2029.

“Our approach is generally going to be long-term focused,” Vinod said. “That’s our inclination always. So keep winning, take a long-term approach, and learn a lot.”
